Writing Tip: Using the First Conditional to Write About Warnings and Threats

You use the First Conditional with if clauses to exchange opinions about possible future outcomes.
The First Conditional with an if clause is also used to convey a warning or a threat in a formal letter.

You use the First Conditional to say it's possible that you will or will not do something. In that condition, something else may, may not, will, or will not happen.
You use the First Conditional to focus on a warning or a threat, especially in the case of a customer complaint or a warning letter.
The parts of the sentence are divided into two clauses: the If clause and the Condition clause.

Structure:
If + Present Simple … will + verb …

Read the following examples from the text:
Finally, I told her that if we eat these meals, we will get sick and sue the restaurant.
If I don't receive a response within three days, I will contact the  food safety authority.
If there isn't a food related incident at your restaurant in the next month, I will be surprised.
If you don't change your business practices, you will be out of business in a year.
Using Verbs, Nouns and Adjectives to Express Purpose
Besides using linking clauses to express your purpose, you can use certain verbs, nouns or adjectives to achieve the same effect.

When you want to express purpose and intention, the following words and expressions can be used.

  • Verbs
    I mean/plan/intend/aim/hope to see you next week.
  • Nouns
    My goal/intention/dream/purpose/hope/aim is to become a professional dancer.
  • Adjectives
    I'm eager/determined/resolved/tempted to call the authorities right now!

Read the following examples from the text, and notice how a letter of complaint needs to have a strong sense of purpose and intention to carry its message:
After this experience, I have no intention of ever setting foot in your establishment again. I am eager to speak with you directly about this experience.
Furthermore, I intend to post my grievances  online if I don't hear from you.
Believe me,  I'm eager to express my views to the public.

images.text:
General Manager
Bistro 88
348 Welling St.
Cambridge, Massachusetts
October 25th

Dear Ms Wright,

I was a customer who recommended your restaurant to clients during their recent stay in Boston.
Unfortunately, the sub-standard food quality and incompetent service we experienced reflected poorly not only on my own personal judgement but also on Cambridge's ability to deliver a world-class dining experience.

Our table should have realized the incompetence of your kitchen staff the minute they received their appetizers, or should I say, some of their appetizers. For those who received their meals on time, the tuna tartare was tasteless and pale in color. The rest of the group were told that the restaurant had sold out of fresh mussels. They resigned themselves to overpriced caesar salads.
The main course tasted equally bad. There was one overriding factor. They were all stone cold and undercooked! When I expressed my concerns to an idle waitress, she appeared bewildered and confused. Finally, I told her that if we eat these meals, we will get sick and sue the restaurant. With that, she turned and marched towards the kitchen in tears.

Shortly after, we spotted the same waitress removing her socks and shoes in the dining room. That was the last straw. In the end, we placed cash on the table for the appetizers and drinks. We were not prepared to put up with such a circus any longer.
After this experience, I have no intention of ever setting foot in your establishment again. I am eager to speak with you directly about this experience.
If I don't receive a response within three days, I will contact the food safety authority. Offering raw chicken and pork to customers is completely unacceptable.

Furthermore, I intend to post my grievances online if I don't hear from you. Believe me, I'm eager to express my views to the public. If there isn't a food related incident at your restaurant in the next month, I will be surprised.
What incompetence!

Sincerely,

Michael Roth
